claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is an example of a multi-component concentrated alloy.
The strength of multi-component concentrated alloys is governed by interactions between dislocations and lattice distortions.
The deformation behavior of multi-component concentrated alloys is governed by interactions between dislocations and lattice distortions.
Alloy composition influences the interaction between dislocations and lattice distortions.
Processing history influences the interaction between dislocations and lattice distortions.
HPT processing combined with thermal treatment introduces lattice distortions.
Lattice distortion and dislocation density are the structural mediators of strength and deformation behavior.
Increasing lattice distortion relative to the as-cast or as-forged baseline will increase strength.
Increasing lattice distortion relative to the as-cast or as-forged baseline will decrease ductility.
The proposed relationships are expected to hold under room-temperature, quasi-static loading.
The proposed relationships are bounded by the specific alloy composition and processing history.
A controlled comparison of as-cast or as-forged material with HPT-processed and thermally treated material can test the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a significant strength increase together with a ductility decrease after introducing lattice distortions would falsify the hypothesis.
